meta.association: Biallelic CLDN1 loss of function causes neonatal ichthyosis-sclerosing cholangitis syndrome (MONDO:0011874), also reported as ILVASC. nodes.description: In the isolated neonatal form, biallelic DCDC2 variants abolish DCDC2 protein, which is normally expressed in cholangiocyte cilia. Affected bile ducts lose not only the protein but the cilium itself, absent on both immunostaining for acetylated alpha-tubulin and transmission electron microscopy. What the cilium contributes to cholangiocyte function is not established by the sources cited here, so this node records the structural loss and the cholangiopathy that accompanies it rather than an intervening functional step. This is a monogenic route into cholangiopathy, distinct from the immune- and microbiome-driven mechanisms modeled for primary sclerosing cholangitis above.

genetic_context.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous DCDC2 variants. No `zygosity` is recorded: the slot is single-valued and has no biallelic value, and this node's own cited quote reports four homozygous and two compound heterozygous patients, so naming either one would contradict the evidence. The series seen at King's College Hospital found only protein-truncating alleles; a second, independent series reported biallelic missense variants and an in-frame deletion in the doublecortin domains, where the protein is mislocalized to the cytoplasm and absent from cilia rather than undetectable. Neither series' geography is asserted here: PMID:27319779's cached record carries no affiliation.

nodes.description: In the syndromic neonatal form, biallelic CLDN1 variants remove claudin-1 from both liver and skin. Claudins are components of tight junctions, which in the liver separate bile flow from plasma, and the founding study proposes that lack of claudin-1 raises paracellular permeability between epithelial cells and that the bile-duct injury follows from its absence in cholangiocytes. That mechanism is the authors' proposal and is carried here with the same hedge. Claudin-1 is absent from skin as well as liver in affected patients, and this subtype is the one distinguished clinically by ichthyosis.

genetic_context.description: Biallelic CLDN1 loss of function. `HOMOZYGOUS` is recorded here, unlike on the DCDC2 node above, because it is the state the sources report: PMID:37814412 states that most ILVASC cases described to date were attributed to homozygous truncating variants, and the founding report described a 2-bp deletion in exon 1 in inbred kindred, producing a premature stop codon and complete absence of claudin-1 protein. The later founder missense allele p.Arg81His segregates in North African Jewish families; the cited record does not state its zygosity, so the slot carries the modal reported state rather than a claim about every described case.

meta.association: Biallelic DCDC2 variants cause isolated neonatal sclerosing cholangitis (MONDO:0018816). DCDC2 is expressed in the primary cilium of cuboidal cholangiocytes; affected patients lose both the protein and the cilium, so the subtype is classified as a liver-based ciliopathy. Two independent series reported different allele classes with the same ciliary phenotype: protein-truncating variants in a series seen at King's College Hospital, and biallelic missense variants or an in-frame deletion in the doublecortin domains in a second, independent series. Only the King's College attribution is sourced - PMID:27469900's full text states it - and no geography is asserted for the other series.
